column1: # Environment keys the pinned engine touches, at revision b4e3a9056567ed8145fc4fa29850d6f1f261ac2b.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The lane admits environment variables by allow list, so
# exhaustiveness is structural and this table is not what makes the lane safe --
# a key missing from here is still refused. Its job is narrower and it is the
# only thing that does it: it is the record that lets a test prove no PERMITTED
# entry in lane.rs names a key the engine itself reads or writes. A permit rule
# that overlaps an engine key silently hands an operator a knob on the forward
# pass while the replica keeps publishing the same configuration digest, which
# is precisely the failure the allow list exists to prevent.
# Derived by sweeping the engine tree at the pin for CAMELID_* string literals.
# It is a snapshot of one revision, not a live view: it is correct only for the
# ENGINE_PIN above and must be regenerated in the same change that bumps it.
# WHAT THIS FILE CANNOT SEE, AND WHY IT MATTERS. Every row here is a CAMELID_
# name, so every test built on it reasons inside one namespace. A lever the
# engine reaches through somebody else's crate -- the data-parallel pool's own
# variables, the platform BLAS pool's -- is not in this corpus and cannot be, so
# no assertion against it will ever surface one. That is not a gap to close by
# widening the sweep: the set of environment names an arbitrary dependency reads
# is not enumerable from this tree, and a corpus that pretended otherwise would
# be worse than one whose boundary is written down. It is written down because
# it already cost something. RAYON_NUM_THREADS was refused while its live
# deprecated alias RAYON_RS_NUM_CPUS was not, and the whole suite stayed green
# over the gap for exactly this reason. lane.rs's REFUSED_FOREIGN rows are
# established by reading the crate that honours the name, at the version this
# workspace pins, and re-read whenever that pin moves. Nothing mechanical here
#   class      READ         read at least once by engine code
#              WRITE_ONLY   only written by engine code (see execution_plan.rs,
#                           whose planner set_var/remove_var's its managed keys
#                           at model load -- after the lane's startup scan)
#              MENTION_ONLY appears only in a string or a computed key fragment
#   first_site  engine-relative path:line of the first occurrence
#   site_count  number of read sites (0 for the non-READ classes)
# Class is deliberately coarse. Anything other than DOC_ONLY means the name is
# spoken for by the engine and must not appear on the lane's allow list.
# CLASS IS SWEPT, THEN CORRECTED BY HAND. The sweep classifies by what sits next
# to the literal, so it scores a key as unread whenever the engine reaches the
# read through a helper -- a name returned from a function, or one assembled at
# runtime from a role string. Seventeen rows were corrected that way and they
# point first_site at the read, not at the literal the sweep found.
# The first ten: CAMELID_APPLE_ACCELERATE (read behind a flag helper), the two
# CAMELID_ZERO_*_DELTA keys (names returned from a match, then read), and the
# seven CAMELID_RECTANGULAR_LINEAR_LAYOUT* keys (the per-role names are built
# with format! and read through the built string, which is exactly why an
# exact-name ban list could never have covered this family).
# Seven more, found by re-checking the classes rather than the names, all of
# them read through one of the engine's boolean-flag helpers -- which take the
# key as an argument, so the literal at the call site does not sit next to an
# env::var and the sweep scored it WRITE_ONLY or MENTION_ONLY with site_count 0:
# the q8 flag helpers in inference/q8_runtime.rs); CAMELID_Q8_SCHED_TELEMETRY
# through a named const rather than the literal.
# Those seven were WRITE_ONLY or MENTION_ONLY, not DOC_ONLY, so no assertion was
# wrong while they sat that way: the overlap guard filters DOC_ONLY only. They
# were corrected because the OTHER guard, every_canonical_key_is_read_by_the
# _engine, selects on class == "READ" -- so a canonical key misfiled the same way
# would make that test pass while proving nothing, which is the same failure
# After those corrections no row is DOC_ONLY. That matters more than it looks:
# DOC_ONLY is the one class the overlap guard filters out, so a key misfiled
